WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
To Rehum and Shimshai: "Give ye now commandment to cause these men to cease, and that this city be not builded, until another commandment shall be given from me." Ezra 4:21

"Artaxerxes, king of kings, unto Ezra the priest, a scribe of the law of the God of heaven, perfect peace"; "for why should there be wrath against the realm of the king and his sons?" Ezra 7:12 Ezra 7:23
Ezra: "Blessed be the LORD God of our fathers, which hath put such a thing as this in the king’s heart, to beautify the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem." Ezra 7:27
Nehemiah: "And the king granted me, according to the good hand of my God upon me." Nehemiah 2:8
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
His letter to Ezra gave silver and gold for offerings, vessels for the house, supplies from the treasurers beyond the river, and freedom from toll for priests and Levites. Ezra 7:15–24
He first halted the building of the city; later he gave Nehemiah letters for timber "for the gates of the palace" and "for the wall of the city". Ezra 4:21 Nehemiah 2:8
He sent letters to "the governors beyond the river", and Ezra delivered "the king’s commissions unto the king’s lieutenants". Nehemiah 2:7–9 Ezra 8:36
He told Ezra to set magistrates and judges for all the people beyond the river who knew the law of his God, and to teach those who did not. Ezra 7:25–26
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
Each mark sits at the year of the reign the Bible gives for it.
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Seventh, twentieth and thirty-second years named; no length of reign.
ARTAXERXES I: LATE 465 – DECEMBER 424 BC (PARKER AND DUBBERSTEIN, 1942)
On this identification his seventh year was 458/457, his twentieth 445/444 and his thirty-second 433/432 BC.
ARTAXERXES I: 465–424 BC (RYLE, 1893)
Ryle: "Artaxerxes reigned 41 years (465–424 b.c.)"; the twentieth year, 445 BC.
ARTAXERXES II: 404–358 BC (FOR ONE VIEW OF EZRA)
Cowley's dates for Artaxerxes II; on this view Ezra's seventh year would be 398/397 BC.
No: the Magian who reigned between Cambyses and Darius
James Ussher (1658); H. Ewald (as reported by R. Dick Wilson, 1915)
Ussher identified this "Artachshashta" with the Magian usurper who called himself Smerdis, so that the work stopped until Darius's second year (Ezra 4:24). Ezra 4:24 [25][12]
Yes: Artaxerxes I
R. Dick Wilson (1915)

Wilson notes there is no evidence that the Magian was ever called Artaxerxes, holds that Artaxerxes I is meant, and says the other view "would never have been thought of had it not been for the difficulty of explaining the reference to him in this place". Ezra 4:12 [12]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say which Persian Artaxerxes is meant, or whether one king is meant throughout.
Nehemiah 2:6 does not name the queen who sat by the king.
Scripture records no separate decree lifting the halt of Ezra 4:21; the next word of the king on the walls is Nehemiah's letters (Neh 2:7–8).
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the textEzra 4:7–23, Ezra 7–8 and Nehemiah 2, 5 and 13 all name "Artaxerxes"; whether one king is meant in all of them is a question below. Ezra 4:7 Ezra 7:1 Nehemiah 2:1

Scholars' viewScholars identify Nehemiah's Artaxerxes with Artaxerxes I, who reigned 465–424 BC; A. Cowley (1923) argued from an Elephantine letter of 408 BC that Nehemiah's "two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes" was 433 BC.[12][6][34]
